item.title: Nvidia Opens Investigation Into Jensen Huang’s Relationship With Suspected Chinese Spy
item.description: Mr. Huang, the company’s chief executive, acknowledged on Sunday that he was intimate with a business executive who U.S. officials had determined was working for Chinese intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Tripp Mickle, Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan, Julian E. Barnes and Ana Swanson
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, is one of the most powerful figures in the artificial intelligence revolution as well as an influential ally of President Trump.

item.title: Rubio Warned Officials About Nvidia Chief’s Entanglement With Chinese Spy
item.description: The secretary of state’s role in drafting a secret memo highlights how top officials were concerned by this past spring about Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan, Julian E. Barnes and Tripp Mickle
item.category: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China
item.media:credit: Lisi Niesner/Reuters
item.media:description: A memo circulated this past spring warning top Trump administration officials that Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

item.title: Microsoft’s Buyout Offer Sets Its Workforce on Edge
item.description: As Microsoft pours billions into artificial intelligence, the company has offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees. The work force was already on edge.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Tara Anand

item.title: What Shaped Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s Thinking on A.I.
item.description: Some call him a doomer. Others see him as a responsible technologist. Here’s how Dario Amodei’s thinking on artificial intelligence was shaped.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac, Kalley Huang, Cade Metz and Georgia Gee
item.media:credit: Ūla Šveikauskaitė

item.title: Giant Merger of NextEra and Dominion Could Fail Amid Anger Over Electricity Bills
item.description: State leaders and residents in Virginia have opposed NextEra’s acquisition of Dominion Energy, fearing that it will accelerate rate increases.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:credit: Mike Kropf/Richmond Times-Dispatch, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Opponents of a merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy demonstrating outside a hearing on Thursday in Richmond, Va.

item.title: Is Jensen Huang Too Powerful to Be Punished by Nvidia?
item.description: The chief executive has a tight grip on his company, presenting a challenge for Nvidia’s board, which is investigating his affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Kalley Huang and Tripp Mickle
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jensen Huang is Nvidia’s biggest individual shareholder. His children are also senior executives at the company.

item.title: What to Know About Nvidia’s Investigation of CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of the A.I. chip company, admitted to a romantic relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence says was recruited by China’s top spy agency.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: “I was unfaithful to my wife,” Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, said in a message to the company. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

item.title: Jeffrey Wigand, Who Blew the Whistle on Big Tobacco, Takes a Lot of Calls
item.description: Jeffrey Wigand, who took on Big Tobacco, counsels insiders who think they have a story about wrongdoing. There are quite a few of them.
item.dc:creator: David Streitfeld
item.media:credit: Taylor Ballek for The New York Times
item.media:description: Jeffrey Wigand at home in Mount Pleasant, Mich.

item.title: Researchers Identify Suspicious Activity on Kalshi and Polymarket Before Times/Siena Poll Release
item.description: A trader placed well-timed bets on Polymarket and Kalshi in two Senate races. It was unclear if the person had access to inside information or simply made good trades.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy and Stuart A. Thompson
item.media:credit: The New York Times

item.title: F.A.A. to Phase Out Floppy Disks in Air Traffic Control Towers
item.description: Decades after the computer industry moved on, federal officials plan to finally ground the once-vaunted tech relic at the nation’s air traffic control centers.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather
item.media:credit: Mark Makela for The New York Times
item.media:description: The floppy disk, once a heralded computer storage technology, will be phased out at the Federal Aviation Administration.

item.title: Why the Tech Right Lost Big This Week
item.description: “This felt like a decidedly anti-tech election.”
item.dc:creator: Max Read, Erin Griffith, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Diane Wong

item.title: Tired of Slow TikToks? This Content Creator Gives You the Ending
item.description: Videos on social media often save key details for the end. One content creator, who goes by Heyitsyoon, skips the filler so viewers don’t have to wait.
item.dc:creator: Victor Mather

item.title: House G.O.P. Leaders Ask Nvidia’s Huang to Speak in Closed-Door Briefing
item.description: The New York Times reported last week that Mr. Huang had a close relationship with an executive that U.S. officials determined was funneling information to Chinese intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Tripp Mickle
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: A request for Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, to speak represented a shift for Republican congressional leaders, who have largely taken a hands-off approach to the tech industry.

item.title: Google, Meta and TikTok Sue California Over Ban on Features for Kids
item.description: Separate lawsuits were filed by Google, Meta and TikTok, which have been battling a flood of claims that their services are addictive.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:credit: Matt Cardy/Getty Images
item.media:description: A new California law says features like personalized recommendations can be “psychologically exploitative” for minors and cause them to check social media compulsively.

item.title: OpenAI Pledges to Give Locals More Say in Data Center Projects
item.description: The artificial intelligence company pledged to be more collaborative with the communities where it is building its data centers.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Scott Ball for The New York Times
item.media:description: OpenAI’s Stargate data center project in Abilene, Texas, is one of the largest under construction in the country.

item.title: Parents Sue Google Over A.I. Safety Risks on School Chromebooks
item.description: A student made plans to end her life after chatting with Google’s artificial intelligence, a new lawsuit claims, amid mounting concerns about online harms to children.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Singer
item.media:credit: Kelsey McClellan for The New York Times
item.media:description: The new lawsuit argues that Google’s “sprawling digital ecosystem” of school laptops and apps has helped the tech giant push its A.I. into classrooms.

item.title: Tech Billionaires Face Tricky Political Waters After Democratic Midterm Sweep
item.description: Many donated money to President Trump’s favored causes and became his allies. Now that political alignment may be a liability.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan, Theodore Schleifer and Erin Griffith
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump met with leaders of the artificial intelligence industry at the White House in September.

item.title: Amazon Kindle Colorsoft Review: The Single-Task Gadget of Our Times
item.description: E-book reader sales are soaring as consumers seek technology offering respite from social media and artificial intelligence hype. It’s even better in color.
item.dc:creator: Brian X. Chen
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times

item.title: Voters Rejected A.I. in the Midterms. Now Comes an Era of Scrutiny.
item.description: After two years of little A.I. oversight, voters on Tuesday rejected data center projects and swept into office Democratic candidates who promised to regulate the technology.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang and Sophia June
item.media:credit: Jon Cherry/Getty Images
item.media:description: A sign supporting the banning of data centers is posted outside a home in New Albany, Ohio.

item.title: Sherrod Brown’s Win in Ohio Is a Rare Loss for Crypto Under Trump
item.description: Fairshake, the major industry super PAC, spent $46 million on ads against the Democrat, Sherrod Brown, who won.

item.media:credit: Maddie McGarvey for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sherrod Brown at the Democratic watch party in Columbus, Ohio, on Tuesday after winning back his Senate seat.

item.title: Voting Problems Cause a Surge in Misleading Fraud Claims Online

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Set Up ‘War Rooms’ to Fight Disinfo About Midterm Elections
item.description: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday’s elections from efforts to undermine democracy.

item.media:description: OpenAI employees work inside the company’s Election Operations Center in San Francisco.

item.title: Binance Says Hackers Plotted $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist for Months
item.description: A report from the cryptocurrency exchange described a monthslong campaign involving fake job interviews that exploited an engineer’s work computer and an internal A.I. tool.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Gabby Jones/Bloomberg
item.media:description: The hackers used a computer and an internal A.I. tool to take control of the machines of two engineers on Binance’s wallet team.

item.title: Apple’s Profit Grows 12% Despite Component Price Worries
item.description: The company said iPhone sales remained strong, but warned that the cost of memory chips for its devices was going up.

item.media:description: Apple’s new touch-screen MacBook Pro at a product launch in Los Angeles last week.

item.title: Are Freezers Being Hacked? Europe and the U.S. Military Investigate.
item.description: A wave of disruptions at grocery stores, which some officials blame on cyberattacks, highlights the vulnerability of supply chains. Shops across Europe were affected again on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Ali Watkins
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Fred Tanneau/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Shelves were empty at a grocery store in Névez, France, last month after hundreds of supermarket refrigeration systems in the country were targeted.
